sections.h2: Which Screven County offices send and set the tax?
sections.html:
Every Screven bill passes through two desks. Valuation belongs to the Board of Tax Assessors. Billing, receipts and tag work belong to the elected commissioner, whose FAQ says the office also handles timber and mobile home accounts.

  • Tax Commissioner, 216 Mims Road #103, Sylvania, GA 30467. Phone 912-564-2206. The counter opens weekdays at 8 a.m. and closes at 4:45 p.m.
  • Tax Assessors, 912-564-7918, for returns, value questions and homestead forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: your recorded deed is kept in the courthouse deed room.

The state revenue department's Screven fact sheet says some cities collect their own levy through a city clerk. Find out from the commissioner whether yours does.

sections.h2: What do Screven County's numbers say about selling a house?
sections.html:
Screven is rural. Its 645.78 square miles hold about 22 people for each square mile, and the July 2025 estimate of 14,408 is 2.5 percent over the April 2020 base of 14,061. The tax office is in Sylvania.

The Census QuickFacts table counts 4,932 households and 6,640 housing units. Homes with a resident owner make up 69.8 percent. A typical owner-occupied house is worth $124,300, the monthly rent is $679 at the midpoint, and household income at the midpoint is $52,792. Persons 65 and over are 23.7 percent of the county, the highest share of the four places covered here. Poverty is 21.1 percent.

Building activity is thin: 19 permits were issued in 2025, and 89.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Few homes change hands, so a house that has sat vacant after a death or move is easy to spot. Bills are small next to metro Georgia, yet an unpaid year stays with the parcel and keeps collecting interest.

sections.h2: What are the due dates in Screven County, GA?
sections.html:
The office posts two different dates, so go by the one printed on your own bill. One page puts real estate and business personal property due on November 15 from 2018 on. Another puts the deadline at December 20.

Late rules posted on the Screven County Tax Commissioner's website
Where postedDueCharges after the date
FAQ pageNovember 15Interest of 1 percent a month, plus a one-time 10 percent charge at 90 days
General information pageDecember 20Monthly interest of prime plus 3 percent over 12, and 5 percent added every 120 days, to a ceiling of 20 percent
Mobile homesApril 110 percent penalty

Under the state fact sheet, interest cannot start until 60 days after the bill is postmarked. When you mail a check, the Postal Service postmark is the proof of timeliness. Metered stamps are refused. Phone the counter for a current balance.

sections.h2: What does a Screven County lien or levy look like?
sections.html:
A month after the due date the office may record a fi. fa., which is a lien, in the superior court clerk's books. Credit bureaus read those books, and the commissioner states that it cannot steer what they do with the entry.

The next stage hands the account to a contractor named DTSi. Administration and levy charges of $215.00 or more land on the bill, covering certified mail and a title search. The house is posted and photographed, and an ad runs for the four weeks ahead of a sale in a newspaper, the Sylvester Local, at the owner's expense.

Clear it before listing, because the buyer's title search will find it.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Screven County valuation?
sections.html:
Assessors set fair market value for each January 1 and tax 40 percent of it. Owners get a window until April 1 to return their own opinion of value. If the assessors reject it, they mail a notice, and 45 days start to run from its date.

  • Pick the county Board of Equalization or arbitration for the hearing.
  • To go further, send written notice that you want Superior Court.
  • Valid grounds are taxability, value and uniformity. How much tax the commissioner bills is not one of them.

Skipping a return you were required to file costs 10 percent of whatever value you left off. The same site gives a mobile home owner 21 days to carry a corrected value to the equalization board. Where the owner is deployed, a friend or relative may file on their behalf, with 90 days from the value notice.

sections.h2: Which Screven County homestead and relief programs matter?
sections.html:
To qualify you must own and occupy the house as of January 1. Paperwork goes to the assessors, and it counts for that year only if received ahead of April 1; later forms start the next year. Bring the warranty deed if this is your first house. Approval carries forward on its own until you move, retitle or ask for another type.

The county has its own local exemptions, and where a local amount tops the state amount it takes over. A further exemption opens at age 62. Separately, the state deferral program lets a homeowner of 62 or more with gross income no higher than $15,000 postpone the tax, with the balance coming due at a transfer or once it hits 85 percent of market value.

Qualifying farm tracts are assessed at 30 percent instead of 40, and conservation use tracts at their use value. Both need a covenant to keep the use for ten years.

sections.h2: How are mobile homes taxed in Screven County?
sections.html:
The commissioner treats a mobile home as personal property. One standing here on New Year's Day owes tax by April 1 and must register at the assessors, collect a location permit and display a decal. Falling behind can draw a 10 percent penalty, a summons to Magistrate Court or even a sale of the unit.

Mobile home bills usually go out near January 2. The state sheet adds that a new placement needs its permit inside 30 days.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Screven County house that has unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Yes. Your closing attorney asks the commissioner for a payoff, and the closer pays it from what you receive at the table. A recorded fi. fa. must be released so the buyer can take clean title.

Cash buyers suit inherited, empty or worn houses, since no lender inspection stands in the way. Set any offer beside a listing price less repairs and a slower close.

faqs.q: Does Screven County want its tax in November or December?
faqs.a: Both dates appear on the commissioner's site, November 15 on the FAQ and December 20 on the general information page. Your bill's printed date rules, and 912-564-2206 can confirm it.

faqs.q: Where does a Screven homeowner file for homestead?
faqs.a: At the Tax Assessors' office, 912-564-7918. Forms that arrive by April 1 count for that year.

faqs.q: How soon must a Screven value dispute be filed?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors hear it first, and then the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: What does a Screven mobile home owner pay each spring?
faqs.a: The year's tax falls due April 1 together with the location permit, and a missed date adds a 10 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Can an older Screven owner postpone the tax?
faqs.a: Yes, at age 62 or more with gross household income of $15,000 or less. The postponed amount stays owed and comes due at a transfer or when it reaches 85 percent of market value.
